idiom_name: typeclass instance (given) + TypeTest for erased abstract types
implementation_notes: Scala's primary answer to 'one interface, unrelated types' is a typeclass - a trait plus a given/instance - or an intersection of traits, not a hand-rolled erasure wrapper; because JVM generics are erased, testing or matching an abstract type parameter requires an explicit witness, and scala.reflect.TypeTest (Scala 3, replacing ClassTag/TypeTag from Scala 2.13) supplies exactly that. TypeTest also replaces the unsound ClassTag.unapply test, which could check only the class component of a type. Structural types (a refinement such as { def close(): Unit }) are the other form: in Scala 3 they require the target to extend Selectable and compile to ordinary code, instead of the reflective proxies Scala 2 used.
pitfalls: ClassTag-based tests are unsound for parameterised types (case _: List[Int] passes for any List); Scala 3's TypeTest replaces them and the compiler warns on the old form.

Typeclass instances resolve at compile time: once a value is typed as Any its instance is gone, so the behaviour must travel with the value (an existential or wrapper) or be recovered through an explicit witness.

Scala 2 structural types needed scala.language.reflectiveCalls with per-call reflection, and Scala 3's Selectable only allows declared members - portable structural code should name a shared trait instead.
